 Student Internship Program
 Student Internship Program dn 2026-09-30T14:01:50-04:00 
 Intern to Serve Your Country
 The U.S. Department of State Student Internship Program is a paid internship with the opportunity to work in embassies and field offices throughout the world, as well as in various bureaus located in Washington, D.C.  This program is designed to provide substantive experiences in a foreign affairs environment.  While the duties of participants vary from bureau to bureau and office to office, it is not uncommon for participants to:   
 Join meetings with senior-level U.S. government or foreign government officials;   
 Draft, edit, or contribute to cables, reports, communications, talking points, or other materials used by policymakers in furthering U.S. foreign policy objectives;   
 Support events, including bilateral, international and/or multilateral meetings and conferences; and/or   
 Engage directly with U.S. audiences to explain the work of the Department of State or with foreign audiences to advance U.S. foreign policy and improve understanding of U.S. culture and society. 
 Benefits 
 Paid interns receive compensation as a GS-04/Step 1 under the base pay schedule and are considered a temporary employee of the U.S. Department of State.  Internship service is not creditable for retirement benefits unless and until the intern is subsequently appointed into a federal career position.  The program covers reasonable travel expenses to and from the Washington D.C. orientation and internship location, as well as provides furnished housing.   
 Please sign up to receive updates for upcoming program cycles and for ongoing updates related to the program.   
 Eligibility Requirements 
 To be eligible for the U.S. Department of State Student Internship Program, you must:   
 Be a United States citizen at the time of application.   
 Be at least 18 years old at the time of application.   
 Be able to receive and maintain a Secret security clearance .   
 Have not previously participated in the U.S. Department of State’s Student Internship Program, U.S. Foreign Service Internship, or Foreign Service Fellowship Program.   
 Be able to show proof of medical insurance during the time of the internship, including the time of travel to and from the location of the internship and international insurance coverage if placement is overseas.   
 Assume responsibility for covering personal medical and health-related expenses during the internship, including maintaining appropriate health insurance coverage.   
 Meet one of the following educational eligibility criteria:  Be a current undergraduate student who has completed at least 60 credit hours by the start of the internship; be a current graduate student; have graduated from an accredited undergraduate or graduate program within two years of the internship start date; or be a veteran of the United States Armed Forces who has served on active duty within the two years preceding the internship start date.   
 Be enrolled at least part-time at the time of application, if applying as a current undergraduate or graduate student.  Breaks in enrollment of up to five months are permitted.   
 Be in good academic standing with a minimum 3.2 GPA, or have earned a minimum 3.2 GPA if applying as a recent graduate.  Possess a high school diploma or equivalent, if applying as a U.S. military veteran.   
 Internship Assignments 
 Most U.S. Department of State Student Internship Program opportunities are offered at the bureau level in Washington, D.C.  Students can work in one of the many offices which make up the respective geographic or functional bureaus or at a post overseas.    
 Learn which office is right for you.   
 Application Process and Timeline 
 Applicants should visit USAJobs and search for the U.S. Department of State Student Internship Program.  New users must create a USAJOBS account and build a resume using the USAJOBS Resume Builder, as uploaded resumes cannot be used for the Department of State application.  From the vacancy announcement, select Apply Online , choose your USAJobs resume, complete all five application sections (Eligibility, Series Grade Questions, All Grade Questions, Documents, and Application Review), and attach an official or unofficial transcript showing proof of student status.  Applications without a successfully attached transcript will be rated ineligible.  Applications may be edited until the announcement closes, after which no changes can be made.  Applicants should review all eligibility requirements carefully, as some questions are exclusionary.     
 Selection Process:     
 The Student Internship Program team reviews eligible application packages and forwards them to the Selection Committee.   
 The Selection Committee identifies finalists and recommends host bureau placements based primarily on Department needs, while considering applicants’ interests and career aspirations when possible.   
 The Student Internship Program team confirms selections and coordinates notifications.   
 Finalists and alternate selectees receive conditional offer letters.   
 Finalists and alternates begin the medical and security clearances process with the Bureau of Medical Services and the Bureau of Diplomatic Security respectively.  Once a finalist receives the required clearance, the Student Internship Program team issues a final offer identifying the assigned host bureau.  If a finalist does not receive a clearance or declines the offer, a cleared alternate may be offered the position.
